newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen hit new highs on Nikkei plunge.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen hit new highs on Nikkei plunge.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures reached new contract highs on Thursday as a sharp drop in Tokyo stock prices reinforced market views that Japan would retain its current low-rate policy into the foreseeable future.
"I heard Euroyen being bought as the Nikkei started coming off," said a trader with a Japanese futures house.
Bearish technicals coupled with poor sentiment pulled the 225-share Nikkei average down 522.36 points to close at a low for the year of 19,570.67.
Dealers said vague rumours that a second-tier Japanese securities house had suffered trading losses contributed to a heavy sell-off in Japanese financial and brokerage stocks.
June Euroyen was quoted at 99.40 at 1115 GMT after hitting a new high of 99.41 against its IMM close at 99.36. September was at 99.30 against 99.25.

"I would sell September Euroyen if it got to 99.35. That's more than half a year from now," said the trader, noting there was no guarantee interest rates would remain at their present lows into the third quarter of 1997.
Comments by senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara that the deregulation of Japan's forex transactions was likely to be implemented on April 1, 1998 had little impact.
"With that kind of timeframe, anything could happen between now and then," said a trader with a U.S. house.
Japanese government bond (JGB) futures for March settled at 126.07 against their previous 125.49.
Eurodollar futures ended little moved on a lack of new leads, and dealers said there was little interest in the U.S. international trade data for October, due at 1330 GMT.
"The immediate trend for Eurodollars would be slightly bearish after two days of selling," said the trader at the U.S. house, adding however, that March Eurodollars would be supported around 94.40.
"There'll be selling on the upside at the 94.46-94.50 level," he added.
The March contract finished at 94.41 against its IMM close at 94.42.
